title: Sinking Trump Approval Ratings Threaten GOP Midterm Hopes, NBC Poll Finds
snippet: A new NBC News survey highlights growing Republican vulnerabilities heading into the midterms, driven by voter frustration over high prices, the conflict with Iran, and President Trump's second-term record.
content:
WASHINGTON — Rising consumer prices, a sluggish economy, and frustration over the war in Iran are creating a difficult political landscape for Republicans ahead of the upcoming midterm elections, according to a fresh NBC News survey released Sunday.

President Donald Trump's job approval rating has dropped to 41% among registered voters—a second-term low in the poll—while 56% express disapproval. A 55% majority of voters believe the administration's policies have actively damaged the economy, a noticeable jump from 48% recorded earlier this spring before military action in Iran sent gas prices soaring.

A Narrow Democratic Lead Balanced by Political Maps

Democrats currently hold a 5-point lead on the generic congressional ballot, leading Republicans 50% to 45%. While significant, that margin is notably narrower than the 12-point advantage Democrats carried at a similar point in 2018 prior to regaining the House majority.

Despite the national headwind for the GOP, the battle for Capitol Hill remains heavily contested due to electoral geography. Many key House races and the critical Senate battlegrounds are taking place in traditionally conservative states and districts.

"We have a classic battle between these numbers and the political geography in which this campaign will be decided," said GOP pollster Bill McInturff of Public Opinion Strategies, who co-conducted the survey. "And the Republicans are still standing because of the geography in which this election will be won or lost."

Signature Policies Failing to Resonate

The poll reveals that several of Trump's central proposals are struggling to build momentum with the electorate:

  • Economic Measures: 42% of voters say they are less likely to support a candidate backing last year's sweeping tax and spending legislation, compared to 36% who say they are more likely.
  • Direct Stimulus Proposal: Trump's convention pitch offering $5,000 payments to adults if Republicans maintain control of Congress met widespread skepticism, with 46% saying it makes them less likely to support a candidate versus 21% who feel more inclined.
  • Foreign Policy: 62% of voters state the war in Iran has not been worth the cost, and 57% say they are less likely to vote for candidates who favor the conflict.

Voter Motivation and Brand Weaknesses on Both Sides

Trump himself has become a major driver for voter turnout, particularly among opposition voters. Forty-three percent of voters—including nearly half of independents—say they plan to use their congressional vote to register opposition to the president, marking a 30-year high in the poll's history.

Voters also voiced greater concern over Republicans going too far in supporting Trump (50%) than over Democrats obstructing his agenda (42%).

However, the Democratic Party faces its own branding challenges. Despite holding advantages on key issues like inflation, healthcare, and government corruption, the Democratic brand remains largely unpopular. Only 29% of voters hold a positive view of the Democratic Party, compared to 36% for the GOP.

Democratic pollster Jeff Horwitt of Hart Research Associates noted that the current dynamic reflects public frustration with incumbents rather than overwhelming support for the opposition.

"This speaks more to deep dissatisfaction with Trump and Republicans than a ringing endorsement of Democrats," Horwitt said. "Voters are continuing to look for change."

The NBC News poll surveyed 1,000 registered voters from Sept. 11-15 and carries a margin of error of plus or minus 3.1 percentage points.
